steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Cut slits into top of roast with a paring knife; place garlic slices into slits. Season roast with black pepper and salt.
Place bay leaves in the bottom of a roasting pan; place roast, fat-side up, on top of bay leaves. Combine cider vinegar and thyme in a small bowl; pour over roast.

Bake in the preheated oven until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center reads 145 degrees F (63 degrees C), about 3 hours. Baste drippings frequently over roast while cooking using a baster or spoon.

raw_recipe.headline: Pork Roast with Thyme
raw_recipe.description: This flavor-infused pork roast with thyme recipe studs pork roast with garlic, roasts on a bed of bay leaves, and bastes with cider vinegar and thyme.
raw_recipe.name: Pork Roast with Thyme

review.reviewBody: OK, EVERYBODY, LISTEN UP! If your complaint is that the meat was TOO DRY, then you need to get out your meat thermometer and USE IT! The #1 reason that pork is "dry" is that you have overcooked it! Pork should be done to an internal temperative of 160 degrees. There should be a touch of pink to it. Sorry, some of you are from the old school of NO PINK IN PORK, but that is just simply not true. This was an absolutely DELICIOUS recipe. My teenage son came up from the rec room to inquire what that AMAZING SMELL was! We ALL loved it! I'll be making this again and again! Only substitution I made was using white wine vinegar as I did not have apple cider vinegar on hand.

We really enjoyed this recipe! The preparation was simple and it was cooking in the crock pot within minutes. It was a last minute decision to make this so I had to make a few slight changes. My roast was fresh out of the freezer, so I used the garlic press and spread the garlic on top of the roast. I was a little shy of the total amount of apple cider vinegar so I used balsamic vinegar to make up the difference. I put the crock pot on low & let it cook about 8 hours. Delicious! I used the juices to make gravy, adding some brown sugar to offset the twang of the vinegar. This was an excellent, savory holiday dinner main dish. The recipe is not something for every day, it is something I’ll use for special dinners. Thank you for sharing!

This is fantastic!! As others have said, I kept adding chicken broth and apple cider vinegar to the pan as it evaporated. The au jus was amazing! Don't skip it. Basted it often as well. I added caraway. USE MEAT THERMOMETER so it doesn't dry out. I removed it at 155/160 to let sit. Next time (Oh yes, there will be many, many next times!) I may try it with tenderloin and shake it in a bag with spices and marinate, as suggested here. Wow, thank you for sharing this. I think this would be great with chicken as well.

This is a wonderful, tasty recipe for pork roast. The vinegar and thyme combo makes the meat and vegetables taste amazing! I placed thick chunks of potato and carrot around the roast before pouring the vinegar/thyme combo over all in my crock pot, We will be using this recipe again soon!

This is the first time I've made a pork roast in the oven and the family loved it!
I used a 3 lb roast, slivered an onion on the bottom of the roasting pan then placed the bay leaves on the onions and the roast on top. I only had 1/3 cup of cider vinegar so I topped it up to the 1/2 cup level with balsamic. Covered at 325 deg it was done in about an hour and a half (we're quite a ways above sea level here). After it was done, I wrapped it in foil to keep it warm and moist then made a gravy from the juice using some chicken stock and flour. After it was ready I sliced the roast and swirled it back in the roasting pan before serving with mashed potatoes. Absolutely delumptious

My roast was very small, just over a pound and was done in 45 minutes. Because of the quicker cooking time it didn't brown, no fault of the recipe, so I put it on a baking sheet lined with foil, sprayed it with olive and put it under the broiler for a few minutes. Even though I was using a smaller roast I kept the ingredients the same except for the pepper, I cut that back to 1.2 tsp. I love pork roast cooked with slices of garlic inserted into it but hubs doesn't so I made a paste with the seasonings and massaged that into roast and let it sit in the fridge for a few hours, taking it out one hour before I planned on cooking it. If I make this again I will sear it before roasting.

Great recipe! I had a 3 lb roast and it was finished in 2 hrs. I did keep it covered for the first hour and basted as recommended. It was well done, but tender and did not dry out. I also put a pan of sweet potato and apple chunks tossed in olive oil and sea salt in with it for the last hour, and they turned out perfect with the roast. I also made a gravy with the drippings left in the pan. Definitely doing again - thank you!

I used balsamic vinegar because of the comments that the vinegar was too strong. I like balsamic vinegar quite well and decided if it was too strong that was OK. Well, it wasn't too strong and it was delicious! I did have to shield my eyes the first few times I opened the oven to baste because the vinegar is strong up front, but toward the end I didn't have to. I cooked the 3 lb roast 1.5 hours on convection roast and it was perfect at 165 degrees.

I used fresh rosemary and fresh thyme rubbing the roast with both and placing in a bag for 1 hour before slitting and putting in the garlic. I simply poured the plain vinegar over the roast to begin. Additionally I used foil to make a pan within a pan making it easier to baste.

I served roasted zucchini and brown rice using the left over drippings on the rice. Delicious! My husband loved it and I will definitely make it again.

This is GREAT!! I used my slow cooker and put 4 small bay leaves and 1 onion sliced on the bottom and on top of that I put a 6lb. shoulder blade pork roast with the garlic slivers(a must). I only had 1/4 c. of cider vinegar so to that I added 1/4c of apple cider to make 1/2c liquid. Poured that over the roast and cooked it on high for 7 hrs. The roast came out so tender and juicy, I've never had it like that before and the gravy was out of this world. This will be the only way I'll make a pork roast again. Thank You Teresa for this awesome recipe.

Teresa, thank you for posting this recipe. Talk about the best pork roast ever! I Convection roasted an 8 pound Boston butt at 300 degrees to an internal temperature of 150 degrees, using the seasonings and instructions from your recipe. Removed from oven, covered and allowed to rest for 20 minutes, then sliced and enjoyed. Simply wonderful! Juicy, tender, and tasty.
Made it as directed (for once) and it was wonderful! Cooked some winter vegetables and potatoes in the pan with the roast and served it all up with applesauce.
Delicious. I followed the recipe. It cooked more quickly but I was armed with my thermometer so caught it in time. I used some of the juices to season smashed potatoes, too.

I didnt think it was going to turn out when it was cooking. The smell of it cooking was a no go for me with the vinegar, but I would suffer again to make this. it is the BEST porkloin I've ever made. I loved it, and so did my son and husband who are both picky eaters. 10/10 will cook again.
I followed the recipe to the letter. I couldn't ask for a better pork roast. It turned out great.
Excellent!!!!
I have to say that this was the most tender pork roast that I've ever made! I'll definitely make it again!!
I seared the roast in a French oven coated with rosemary salt and pepper. Roasted at 325 for a few hours and then threw some potatoes in.

This was pretty good, although like others, mine did get a bit dry. I put mine in the crock pot on low for about 7 hours. I probably should have shredded it up a bit after 5 or 6 hours and let it finish cooking in the juices. I think that would have helped it. Otherwise I made as written and it was flavorful. I didn't mind the vinegar at all.
This is a very easy and delicious recipe. The meat was tender and moist. I do use a meat thermometer, and I am careful not to overcook it.
